business_problem: Large enterprises could not see how employees actually used applications and business processes across thousands of SaaS tools, which made it hard to control shadow IT, rationalize licenses, and prioritize AI initiatives with the highest business impact.
solution_summary: Beamy built an AI-driven business transformation platform on Google Cloud to reconstruct how people, technologies, and business processes actually interact inside large organizations. A browser extension captures real-time employee activity such as opening tickets, editing CRM fields, or validating invoices, then transforms those interactions into structured logs. Vertex AI models analyze those logs to identify process patterns across a sprawling application estate, while Cloud Run executes Beamy's serverless application services, BigQuery stores and analyzes large-scale behavior data, and Looker exposes the resulting insights through dashboards for business and IT leaders. This architecture lets customers such as Veolia see the gap between official inventories and real usage, negotiate software spend with evidence, and prioritize more than a thousand AI opportunities based on actual work patterns instead of assumptions.

data_flow: A browser extension observes employee actions across enterprise applications, turns those events into structured logs, analyzes the logs with Vertex AI to reconstruct real business process sequences, stores the behavioral data in BigQuery, and serves prioritized insights to customers through Looker dashboards and Beamy's platform services.
business_outcome: Beamy revealed thousands of previously untracked applications, helped customers rationalize licenses and negotiate spend, and gave enterprises a fact-based way to choose among more than 1,000 candidate AI initiatives.
